clue.text: Return cook's instructions about flipping pancake right

indicators.note: about means the recipe goes around the flipped letters

parts.note: a recipe is the set of instructions a cook follows

indicators.note: flipping turns the pancake and right over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: a taco is a folded Mexican flatbread, loosely a pancake

explanation.surface: A recipe telling the cook to flip a pancake to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the recipe around the flipped letters, splitting it after its fifth letter; calling a taco a pancake is a stretch the setter allows.
explanation.definitionFit: To reciprocate is to give back in kind, so it is a synonym of the verb return.

clue.text: Headless type of beer turned up, designed for older tastes?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards
headless means the first letter of the beer is cut off

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A beer with no froth turns up, styled to appeal to older drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER without its head is ORTER, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styling deliberately imitates the fashions of the past, appealing to older people's nostalgia.

clue.text: Office for National Statistics breaking big survey agreement

indicators.note: breaking means the agency's letters break into the survey, sitting inside it

parts.note: a census is a survey of the whole population
ONS is the abbreviation for the UK's Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: The statistics office wrecking agreement on a major survey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Office for National Statistics is the British body that actually runs the census, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general accord reached by a group, a synonym for agreement.

clue.text: Club, say, coming under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming under means utter is placed below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A club, for example, finding itself under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club, say' looks like one phrase, but 'say' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used on the green for rolling the ball toward the hole.

clue.text: Rich person giving away capital? That's not on

indicators.note: giving away capital means losing the initial letter of the word

parts.note: a toff is British slang for a wealthy, upper-class person

explanation.surface: A rich person handing over money, which is not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money but means the first letter: TOFF loses its T. A toff is a posh, wealthy British person.
explanation.definitionFit: Off is the opposite of on, as with a switch or a cancelled event.

clue.text: Perhaps JFK left after broadcast

indicators.note: after means port is placed following the broadcast word

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Something about John F. Kennedy departing after a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: JFK looks like the president but is New York's airport, so 'Perhaps' signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: JFK is the name of New York's main international airport, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Showing initiative to embark on parking revolution

parts.note: to enter on something is to embark on it
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a rising is a revolt or revolution

explanation.surface: Someone shows initiative by launching a parking revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person is resourceful and ready to undertake new ventures, which is what initiative means.

clue.text: Looking a long way back in case locals are upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the phrase are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking the long historical view in case local people get upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like a link phrase but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoclassical style revives the art of ancient Greece and Rome, harking back two thousand years.

clue.text: No longer with us, former partner can court

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The former partner, now dead, can still go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct describes something that has died out entirely and no longer exists.

clue.text: Initial resistance got round by a bunch of fives

indicators.note: got round by means the fist surrounds the resistance letter

parts.note: a bunch of fives is British slang for a fist (five fingers clenched)
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: First resistance overcome by a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bunch of fives' is old British slang for a punch or fist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something initial comes at the very beginning, as does the first one.

clue.text: What lovers share left in company, stirring senses

indicators.note: in means the left letter goes inside the company abbreviation
stirring means the letters of senses are mixed up

explanation.surface: Lovers, alone in company, feel a stirring of the senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like an adjective for romance but is the anagram signal for the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness is intimacy, the emotional bond two lovers have together.

clue.text: Put on Hamlet, initially with one of those moving scenes?

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Hamlet

parts.note: and means with, along with

explanation.surface: Staging Hamlet, with someone who shifts the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving scenes' sounds like touching drama but means physically shifting scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand works backstage shifting scenery and props between scenes of a play.

clue.text: Blade protected by cardboard

indicators.note: protected by means the word sits wrapped inside cardboard

explanation.surface: A blade kept safe in a cardboard sheath.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar is called its blade, and rowers use blade for the whole oar.

clue.text: Who might paint rocky strait

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters of strait are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who might paint a rocky stretch of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a kind of creative person whose work is pictures.

clue.text: Tons running activity to track virus contacts

parts.note: racing means running fast

explanation.surface: Lots of people dashing around tracking down virus contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls pandemic-era test-and-trace programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact tracing is the public-health work of finding people exposed to an infected person.

clue.text: Minister's early life round queen

parts.note: one's past is one's earlier life
O is round in shape
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A minister's childhood revolving around the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a clergyman in charge of a congregation, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Keep man on board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a keep is the main tower of a ..., a fortress
second meaning: a chess piece, also called the rook

explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a ship's crew but means a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified stronghold, and in chess the rook is commonly called a castle.

clue.text: Son with father in resort

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A son and his father on holiday at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa town is a health resort built around mineral springs.

clue.text: Not so many on express without nationality

indicators.note: on means less comes after the express word

parts.note: to state is to express in words
less means not so many

explanation.surface: Fewer passengers on the express train lacking passports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' reads as a train but is the verb meaning to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateless person is not recognised as a citizen by any country.

clue.text: Correct your setter in conclusion

indicators.note: in means the setter's pronoun goes inside the conclusion word

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The setter making a correction in the final part.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to revise a text by fixing its errors, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Coldness in church, not healthy

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A cold church making people unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a feeling of cold, so it names coldness.

clue.text: Loads of things, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A heap of things, mainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot means a great quantity, so loads of things describes it as a whole.

clue.text: I ranted about item given in part-payment

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about an item offered against the price of a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old article handed over to reduce the price of a new purchase.

clue.text: Flight she had led topless and slightly drunk

indicators.note: topless means each of the four words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman led a topless flight while tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' applies to all four words: LIGHT, HE, AD and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling giddy, as from a little alcohol, is to be tipsy.
